task.description: HARD GATE on REQ-ANALYST's Release 2 draft. Run WF-01 Step 2 checks a-e against each of REQ-033..REQ-041 in docs/agents/requirements.yaml. This is the gate that decides whether Release 2 is buildable, so re-derive independently -- read the requirement text yourself, do not validate against REQ-ANALYST's handoff summary. In particular verify these specific claims REQ-ANALYST made, because each is a checkable factual premise the draft rests on: (1) that REQ-020 (done) genuinely states its refusals are placeholders for Release 2 to fill in, so REQ-034/REQ-038 replacing them is not a contradiction of a done requirement -- read apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts and REQ-020's own text; (2) that no Wishlist table/row is created anywhere in the draft and the wishlist substitution is stated consistently across all five requirements that reference it; (3) that the InviteCode FK deferral REQ-011 recorded is actually picked up by REQ-033; (4) that story coverage is genuinely complete for B6, B7, B8, B9, F3, F4, F9 against USER-STORIES.md's Confirmation bullets and STORY-DETAILS.md's Refuses lines -- a story is not covered because a REQ mentions it, only if its acceptance criteria and refusals are actually testable somewhere. Also check the three ambiguities REQ-ANALYST deliberately left to the design step (FR-4's per-event eligibility flag, FR-17's 'opened' status, nullable registration_closes_at): a deferral is legitimate ONLY if the requirement text forbids silently inventing a resolution and names who resolves it -- if any of them is merely vague instead, that is a testability FAIL.
acceptance_criteria: Checks a (testability), b (consistency), c (depends_on correctness), d (design-system fit), e (size) were each actually run against each of REQ-033..REQ-041, with the finding stated per requirement id.
The four numbered claims in the task description were each independently verified against the cited files, and the verification method is stated -- not asserted.
Any FAIL cites the specific requirement id and which check letter failed.
Story coverage for B6, B7, B8, B9, F3, F4, F9 is confirmed or a gap is named precisely.

result.summary: PASS. All five WF-01 Step 2 checks (a testability, b consistency, c depends_on, d standards fit, e size) were run against each of REQ-033..REQ-041 individually, re-derived from the requirement text in docs/agents/requirements.yaml and the cited source files -- not from REQ-ANALYST's step-01 result.summary. Structural re-derivation: parsed requirements.yaml with PyYAML (the `yaml` node module REQ-ANALYST's summary cites is NOT resolvable in this repo, so that claim was re-run by another means rather than accepted); 42 entries parse, 9 new, every new entry carries id/title/owner/status: pending/description/acceptance_criteria/depends_on, AC counts 7-12 (minimum 2), zero orphaned depends_on, and the dependency graph REQ-032 -> REQ-033 -> {034->035->036->041, 037->038->039, 037->040} is acyclic with all non-new dependencies (REQ-032, REQ-014, REQ-021) at status done. CHECK a TESTABILITY -- PASS for all nine. Every AC names a constructed state, an observable (a row value, a captured message, a grep result, a row count before/after) and a failing condition; ten ACs across REQ-034/035/036/038/039/040/041 explicitly disqualify the weaker run ('a run against an event with seats remaining does not exercise this and is not evidence'), which is core-directives' re-derive-under-the-right-conditions rule written into the requirement itself. No vague predicate ('appropriately', 'as needed', 'looks good') appears in any of the nine. The three deliberate deferrals were held to the handoff's stricter standard (legitimate only if the text forbids inventing a resolution AND names who resolves it) and all three clear it: FR-4 per-event eligibility (REQ-038) enumerates resolutions (a)/(b), states 'It must not add the column silently under either reading', and AC 8 fails if the artefact does not state its choice or if a new events column appears; FR-17 'opened' (REQ-040) enumerates two readings with their observable difference, and AC 5 requires the artefact to state the choice and justify any stored column against PRD 5; nullable registration_closes_at (REQ-036 AC 5, REQ-041 AC 8) names the fallback options, forbids a column, and each AC constructs the NULL case and fails on a crash, an undescribed silent skip, OR a new column, with REQ-041 additionally required to state why if it diverges from REQ-036. 'The design step/artefact' is a real named resolver -- CODE-DESIGNER at WF-02 Step 1 gated by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR at Step 1b (docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md lines 23, 124, 164, 199) -- so each deferral names an agent that exists and a gate that will catch a non-answer. These are bounded choices with a named resolver and a failing condition, not vagueness. CHECK b CONSISTENCY -- PASS for all nine; no conflict with any done requirement or any of the 7 decision records (0001-0007 all read; 0004 framework-free domain logic and 0007 doors-time are the two Release 2 touches and both are honoured, REQ-038 citing 0004 by name). CHECK c DEPENDS_ON -- PASS for all nine, verified semantically, not only for existence. CHECK d -- the handoff directs that the AI Qadam Design System does not meaningfully apply to bot/Telegram work and names the substitutes; I CONFIRM I APPLIED THAT SUBSTITUTION and checked PRD 5's 'if nothing uses it, it is optional' rule, the computed-not-stored boundary, PRD 12's eight invariants and security-invariants.md S1-S14 instead. PASS for all nine; details in the CHECK_D issue entry. CHECK e SIZE -- PASS for all nine; splits checked for a real seam rather than accepted because a split exists; details in the CHECK_E issue entry. All four factual premises named in the task block were independently verified against the cited files (methods stated per claim in the issue entries); three are true as stated, and claim 2's requirement text is correct while REQ-ANALYST's SUMMARY of it overstates by one requirement -- recorded as MINOR, not a FAIL, because the discrepancy is in the producer's summary and not in the gated artefact. Story coverage for B6, B7, B8, B9, F3, F4, F9 is complete: every Confirmation bullet in USER-STORIES.md and every Refuses line in STORY-DETAILS.md traces to a specific numbered acceptance criterion that would fail if the behaviour were absent. VERDICT: PASS -- REQ-033..REQ-041 are ready for WF-02.

issues.description: CLAIM 1 (REQ-020's refusals are placeholders Release 2 fills in, so REQ-034/REQ-038 replacing them is not a contradiction of a done requirement) -- VERIFIED TRUE. Method: read REQ-020's own entry in requirements.yaml rather than REQ-ANALYST's paraphrase. Its description states verbatim: "PRD FR-4's other three rows (requires_approval, and either requires_invite case) belong to Release 2 and are NOT implemented here ... This requirement must nonetheless not make them impossible: the flags exist on Event (REQ-011) and this handler reads them, refusing clearly for a requires_invite or requires_approval event rather than silently admitting." Its sixth acceptance criterion is "Attempting to register for an event with requires_invite=true or requires_approval=true produces a clear refusal naming the reason rather than an admission -- verified by constructing both flags (PRD 4: these are Release 2)", which names Release 2 as the successor in the criterion text itself. Independently confirmed in code: apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts lines 48-49 declare the outcome union members { kind: "requires-invite" } and { kind: "requires-approval" }, and lines 72-77 return them from decideRegistrationOutcome() by reading input.requiresInvite / input.requiresApproval. So the placeholder is real, is reached by a flag read, and REQ-020 pre-authorized its replacement. Check b passes for REQ-034 and REQ-038 on this point.

CLAIM 2 (no Wishlist table/row anywhere in the draft, and the substitution stated consistently across all five referencing requirements) -- THE REQUIREMENT TEXT IS CORRECT; REQ-ANALYST'S HANDOFF SUMMARY OVERSTATES BY ONE. Method: `grep -rni wishlist apps/bot/` returns ZERO matches, confirming no wishlist table, migration or column exists to be contradicted; then grepped 'wishlist' across the REQ-033..REQ-041 span of requirements.yaml and read every hit in context. FINDING: the substitution is DECIDED once in REQ-035's 'WISHLIST OFFRAMP IN RELEASE 2' block and inherited BY NAME and unchanged in REQ-036, REQ-038 and REQ-041, and each of those FOUR carries a zero-match grep AC ('No wishlist table, migration or row is created by this requirement'). REQ-039 carries NO wishlist reference and NO such AC, so the step-01 summary's phrase 'Each of those five requirements carries an AC grepping ... for wishlist' is FALSE as written -- four do, not five. THIS IS NOT A FAIL, and the discrepancy is in REQ-ANALYST's summary rather than in the requirement: I checked whether B8 actually needs an offramp and it does not. STORY-DETAILS B8's Refuses line is exactly 'Reusing a spent code. Storing anything before consent.' -- no 'offered the wishlist' clause anywhere in B8, unlike B6, B7 and B9 which all have one. Both of B8's actual refusals are covered by REQ-039 ACs 6 and 3 respectively. So REQ-039 correctly does not inherit an offramp it has no refusal path for. Recorded per core-directives' never-resolve-a-conflict-silently rule so the inaccuracy is fixed at the source rather than propagating into a later run's premise.

CLAIM 3 (the InviteCode FK deferral REQ-011 recorded is actually picked up by REQ-033) -- VERIFIED TRUE. Method: read apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts directly rather than trusting REQ-033's own quoted 'VERIFIED CURRENT STATE' paragraph, which itself instructs the reader not to trust it. Lines 276-278 read: '// No FK: no InviteCode table exists in this requirement's scope' / '// (REQ-011.md 11 open question 3). A future requirement adds the FK.' / 'inviteCodeId: uuid("invite_code_id"),' -- i.e. a plain uuid column with no references() call, exactly as REQ-033 describes, and the deferral comment is present verbatim. REQ-033 picks it up in its scope ('The FK: registrations.invite_code_id becomes a real foreign key to invite_codes.id, replacing the plain uuid column') and, more importantly, makes it FALSIFIABLE in AC 4, which requires inserting a registration whose invite_code_id names a non-existent invite_codes row and confirming it FAILS, stating explicitly that 'an insert that succeeds proves the FK was not added and is a FAIL of this criterion'. That is a test that can only pass if the deferred half is genuinely closed. Also confirmed no invite_codes table exists yet, so REQ-033 is not redundant.

CLAIM 4 (story coverage genuinely complete for B6, B7, B8, B9, F3, F4, F9 -- acceptance criteria AND refusals actually testable, not merely mentioned) -- VERIFIED TRUE, all 7 covered, all Confirmation bullets and all Refuses lines traced to a specific AC. Method: read each story's Confirmation bullets in USER-STORIES.md and each story's Refuses line in STORY-DETAILS.md, then located the specific AC that would fail if the behaviour were absent; a REQ merely naming a story was not accepted as coverage. B6 -> REQ-034 + REQ-036: 3 Confirmations (pending + told a decision follows = REQ-034 ACs 1-2; approved + notified = REQ-035 AC 1; rejected with reason + notified = REQ-035 AC 2); Refuses 'Requesting twice' = REQ-034 AC 3 (row count after second attempt); the STORY-DETAILS-only 'auto-declined with an honest message' = REQ-036 ACs 2-3. B7 -> REQ-038: 3 Confirmations (valid code admits + used_count increments = AC 1, covering BOTH the i_ deep link and the typed route; expired/spent/unknown told clearly = AC 3, which constructs all four cases including wrong-event; past attendee admitted without a code = AC 7); Refuses 'A code for a different event. A personal code redeemed by someone else' = AC 3's fourth case and AC 2 respectively, AC 2 being the security-sensitive one with its own not-evidence clause. B8 -> REQ-039: 3 Confirmations (admitted + recorded as invited by me = AC 1; full event waitlists = AC 5; second person on a one-use code refused = AC 6); Refuses 'Reusing a spent code' = AC 6, 'Storing anything before consent' = AC 3, which counts users/profiles/registrations rows before and after an abandoned pre-consent flow and disqualifies a run that reached consent first. B9 -> REQ-041: 3 Confirmations (told plainly + offered the onward path = ACs 1 and 6; promoted before then never receives it = AC 3; event ending adds nothing further = AC 5); Refuses 'Sending twice' = AC 4, the kill-and-restart test. F3 -> REQ-035 + REQ-036: 3 Confirmations (list shows each person's relevant details = the request-list rendering plus AC 8's privacy bound; approve admits + notifies = AC 1; reject with reason notifies and is LOGGED = ACs 2 and 10); Refuses 'Approving beyond capacity without an explicit override' = AC 4, which runs both the dismissed and the confirmed branch and counts the audit row; the STORY-DETAILS-only 48h urgency = REQ-036 AC 1, which runs both the at-boundary and the more-than-48h-out timings. F4 -> REQ-037: 4 Confirmations (personal works once and only for that event = AC 1; bulk stops after N = AC 1 with max_uses=N, enforcement itself being REQ-038 AC 3's spent case; companion records the host = AC 1; I can see who has used it = ACs 6-7, AC 7 proving the list is DERIVED by inserting a registration directly and comparing the invite_codes row's updated timestamp); Refuses 'Codes for finished or cancelled events' = AC 5, both constructed with the table re-counted. F9 -> REQ-040: 3 Confirmations (add a never-used guest and issue them a personal code = ACs 1-2, AC 2 specifically proving two NULL tg_id rows coexist; entry shows invited/opened/registered/attended = AC 3 constructing all four states; redeeming links rather than duplicating = AC 6 capturing the pre-created row id and the users count, plus AC 7 for the already-has-an-account case FR-17's 'so nobody is duplicated' makes reachable); Refuses 'Sending on the guest's behalf' = AC 9, a grep for any send path targeting a NULL-tg_id user, restated on REQ-037 AC 9 because that is the other surface where the temptation arises. ADDITIONALLY CHECKED and found NOT a gap: F9's 'active in the Telegram group is where that human judgement gets recorded' sits in STORY-DETAILS' Also and PRD FR-17's 'What this cannot do' paragraph, not in any Confirmation bullet; its normative content is the PROHIBITION 'Do not fake this with a proxy metric', which REQ-040 AC 10 tests by grepping for any engagement score, activity heuristic or group-activity column. No story is covered by mention alone.

CHECK d -- the handoff directs that the AI Qadam Design System does not meaningfully apply to bot/Telegram work and names the substitute standards. I CONFIRM I APPLIED THAT SUBSTITUTION AND STATE WHAT I CHECKED. (1) PRD 5's 'if nothing uses it, it is optional' rule: the one apparent tension is REQ-039 requiring NAME, PHONE and COMPANY from a companion, while PRD 5 line 71 lists phone as currently optional by that rule and says such a field 'must never block a person from finishing what they came to do'. NOT a violation: STORY-DETAILS B8 step 2 specifies the companion 'gives a short profile -- name, phone, company', so phone IS used by a requirement here and thereby earns being required, which is the rule's own test; and done REQ-030 already established this exact reasoning for the walk-in door flow in the same words ('that is not a contradiction, it is the door's own minimum'), which REQ-039 cites by name and reproduces rather than inventing. Consistent with a done requirement, so check b passes on this point too. (2) The computed-not-stored boundary: PRD 5's 'Never stored -- always computed' block names no_show, waitlist position, seats taken, registration_open and finished. REQ-033 AC 9 greps its migration for all five names. REQ-034 adds no capacity column and reasons explicitly that a 'requested' registration does not occupy a seat because seats_taken counts only admission='admitted'. REQ-040 keeps registered and attended derived and proves it in AC 4 by mutating the database directly and asserting the list entry row's updated timestamp is unchanged -- a genuine derivation test, not an assertion. REQ-038 AC 7 forbids a stored returning/attended-before flag by grep. The one stored counter, invite_codes.used_count, is correctly identified as NOT a violation: PRD 5 lists used_count as an InviteCode field in the same block, so it is named data, not a computed value being cached. REQ-040's stored 'invited' is justified as the organizer's own act, which nothing else records, and its 'opened' is deferred rather than silently stored. (3) PRD 12's invariants: 12.1 one Registration per (event,user) -- REQ-034 AC 3; 12.2 seats_taken/capacity with a logged override -- REQ-035 AC 4, REQ-038 AC 6 (a code does not buy past capacity), REQ-039 AC 5; 12.7 every status change writes exactly one AuditLog row -- an explicit counted-before-and-after AC on REQ-034, REQ-035, REQ-036 (with actor_user_id NULL for system-initiated), REQ-037, REQ-038, REQ-039 and REQ-040, and REQ-041 correctly asserts the CONVERSE in AC 10 (zero audit rows, because B9 changes no state and 12.7 is scoped to status changes) -- that inverse is the right reading of the invariant, not an omission, and REQ-041 says so explicitly so it reads as a decision; 12.8 notification idempotency per (registration,kind) -- REQ-036 AC 4 and REQ-041 AC 4, both kill-and-restart tests that disqualify a single-run check. (4) security-invariants.md: S1 consent precedes storage (REQ-038 AC 9, REQ-039 AC 3); S2 authorization on the action with the negative path proven (REQ-035 ACs 6-7, REQ-037 AC 8, REQ-040 AC 11 -- each constructing the callback data directly rather than tapping a rendered button, and each refusing EventStaff, which is S2's named negative case); S3 a member reads only their own Profile (REQ-035 AC 8, REQ-037 AC 6, REQ-039 AC 7, REQ-040 AC 8 -- all four grep the captured output for the actual stored phone and email values); S4 tokens unguessable and single-purpose (REQ-033 ACs 6-7 requiring a CSPRNG, a Math.random grep, a 10000-code collision test and a stated entropy calculation; REQ-034 AC 5 withholding the qr_token until admission); S7 capacity holds (REQ-035 AC 5 and REQ-038 AC 4, both 20-iteration concurrency tests that explicitly reject a sequential test as evidence); S8 (as 12.7 above); S9 idempotency (as 12.8 above); S10 transactional sends reach broadcast_opt_in=false and skip blocked (REQ-035 AC 9, REQ-036 AC 7, REQ-041 AC 9); S11 PII never in plaintext logs (REQ-039 AC 8). No new visual, copy or token pattern is requested by any of the nine, so nothing needs escalating to the design system's owner. Check d PASS on the substituted standards for all nine.

CHECK e SIZE -- PASS for all nine, with the splits checked for a real seam rather than accepted because a split exists. REQ-033 is schema + FK + generator with NO handlers or flow, matching the REQ-010/REQ-011 DATA-DESIGNER precedent for a table serving multiple flows (InviteCode serves B7/B8/F4/F9), and the owner field DATA-DESIGNER is correct for that shape rather than BACKEND-DEV. REQ-034/REQ-035 split the approval flow at the member/organizer boundary, which is a genuine seam: B6 and F3 are two separate USER-STORIES entries and are verified by different means (a row plus a message vs. an organizer action plus an audit row). REQ-036 is correctly separated from REQ-035 because it is scheduled-job work on REQ-025's runner, a different mechanism from a synchronous decision surface, and it legitimately serves two stories because JOURNEY-AUDIT J3 files its deadline rules as criteria on BOTH B6 and F3 rather than as its own story -- folding it into either would push that one past a turn. REQ-037/REQ-038 split issuing from redemption, which STORY-DETAILS F4 itself endorses ('Moves. Nothing directly; drives B7 and B8'). REQ-039 reuses REQ-038's validation path rather than forking one, which is what keeps it small, and USER-STORIES B8 states 'Depends on B7' outright, matching depends_on: [REQ-038]. REQ-040 is the largest at 12 ACs but is one coherent surface (list + entries + derived status + linking) and its code issuing is delegated to REQ-037 rather than duplicated. REQ-041 is the smallest, matching USER-STORIES sizing B9 as S against M for every other Release 2 story. No requirement smuggles in an unrelated second deliverable.

REQ-ANALYST's step-01 result.summary states the file 'parses as valid YAML (verified with the `yaml` parser, 42 entries)'. The `yaml` node module is NOT resolvable from this repository (require('yaml') fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND at the repo root, and there is no node_modules/yaml), so that specific verification claim could not have been run as described. The underlying FACT is nonetheless true -- I re-derived it with PyYAML and confirm the file parses and contains exactly 42 entries, 9 of them new -- so this is a misdescribed method, not a false result, and it does not affect the verdict. Filed per core-directives' No Speculation and never-resolve-silently rules so the producer's habit of naming a tool it did not run is corrected at the source; a future run with a different underlying fact would not be caught by a reader who trusted the stated method.
